headline: Canada Presses Qatar Into Submission; Red Cards Seal the Rout
story: Canada suffocated Qatar with eight high-press phases to Qatar's 0.4. Dominating 66% possession in a relentless 4-4-2, Johnston and Saliba turned the ball over 31 times. Qatar's 21-second ball recovery versus Canada's 8.4 told the tale before the whistles. Red cards for Homam Ahmed (33') and Assim Madibo (51') made it arithmetic rather than sport: nine men against a four-man press, two early Canadian goals already scored.

Canada's xG of 3.9 versus Qatar's 0.2 remained a lie of omission—Qatar never fired. Only two shots, zero on target. Jonathan David (9.8 rating) was untouchable, clinical against an increasingly fractured defence. Even in chaos, Canada squandered chances: xG 0.62 missed at 90+8, xG 0.48 blocked at 38. Six goals from 33 shots reflected both clinical efficiency and Qatar's 20% possession desperately seeking oxygen.

keyMoment.text: Homam Ahmed sent off. From ten men, Qatar's collapse became inevitable; second red at 51' sealed nine.

home.verdict: High-press perfection overcame Qatar; sloppy finishing late was the only scare.
points: Eight high-press phases versus Qatar's 0.4: they never pressed, never competed for the ball
31 forced turnovers against a 21-second ball-recovery time: constant, inescapable suffocation
Jonathan David's 9.8 rating proved clinical when spaces opened; one of the match's best

away.verdict: Two red cards at 33' and 51' ended any contest; but press mismatch meant defeat from kickoff.
points: Ball recovery of 21 seconds—13 seconds slower than Canada's 8.4-second press cycle—meant constant pressure
High-press phases of 0.4 versus Canada's 8: never pressed, never won the midfield back
xG 0.2 on two shots, zero on target: couldn't create, couldn't threaten even at 11 men

statLine: Qatar's 21-second ball recovery versus Canada's 8.4 seconds: the chasm that decided everything before the first red fell.
